article_title: SSTP1, a Host Defense Peptide, Exploits the Immunomodulatory IL6 Pathway to Induce Apoptosis in Cancer Cells

mechanism_summary.topline: SSTP1 anticancer activity is supported as IL6Rα/gp130/JNK/AP1-linked apoptosis/growth inhibition in cancer-cell assays, not as a generic antimicrobial or nonspecific membranolytic mechanism.
downgrade_notes: Antimicrobial activity is not directly assayed in this paper despite database labels.
Exact figure-curve point values not printed in source text were not fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SSTP1 physically associates with IL6Rα-containing receptor complexes on HSC-4 cells and is modeled to bind the active IL6/IL6Rα/gp130 complex; this supports a receptor-linked uptake/signaling mechanism, with docking treated as computational support.
direct_assay_types: FRET analysis of SSTP1 and IL6Rα proximity

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Figure 5 combines co-localization, pull-down, and FRET evidence; Figure 6 docking/MD is computational and not used alone as direct mechanism closure.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct receptor-association evidence for SSTP1 in HSC-4 cells; docking residue rearrangements remain computational/inferred.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SSTP1 shifts IL6-pathway signaling toward JNK/AP1 activation and growth inhibition; JNK, gp130, IL6Rα antibody, and IL6Rα knockdown perturbation experiments support dependence on this receptor pathway.

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: The source reports STAT/JNK/c-JUN blots, AP1 reporter activation, inhibitor effects, and loss of SSTP1 activity after IL6Rα knockdown.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct cell-signaling mechanism evidence in HSC-4 cells; not a general antimicrobial mechanism claim.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SSTP1 induces HSC-4 growth inhibition and early apoptosis with mitochondrial-apoptosis marker activation, while SSTP2 control peptide is comparatively inactive in these assays.

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Source text gives HSC-4 IC50 10.22 μM and early apoptosis increase from 3.8% to 14.9%, with PARP/caspase 3/7/9 cleavage.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Phenotype and apoptosis pathway support; molecular receptor dependence comes from the IL6R/JNK/AP1 claims.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: At low activity-relevant concentration, SSTP1 has limited human RBC hemolysis, supporting the paper’s caution that growth inhibition is not explained only by nonspecific membranolysis.
direct_assay_types: dose-response curve comparison with cancer/HEK293 cells

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: The text reports 5 μM hemolysis as only -0.25% and contrasts low membranolytic activity with MDA-MB-231 IC50 context.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct negative/cautionary mechanism evidence; does not support a high-specificity membrane pore model for anticancer action.

supported_mechanisms: apoptosis/growth inhibition in IL6Rα-expressing cancer cells
cautions: Antimicrobial label is database-level, not directly measured in this paper.
Nonspecific membranolysis is not sufficient to explain low-concentration anticancer activity.

absence_and_boundary_notes: No MIC or bactericidal assay for SSTP1 is reported in this paper.
No exact table of all Figure 1/Figure 10 curve points is present in the local XML/PDF/supplement text.
Docking to the IL6/IL6Rα/gp130 complex is computational and must not be the sole direct mechanism evidence.
adjudicator_summary: Worker-6 replaced automated mechanism locator notes with source-reviewed claims. Strongest support is receptor-linked JNK/AP1 apoptosis/growth inhibition; database antimicrobial labels remain cautionary.
